title: Pocket Flock - Centre for Digital Media project - Buffalo Buffalo
description: A cozy mobile game about birdwatching made in Unity with team Birdbrain as a Centre for Digital Media project for Buffalo Buffalo.
thingsLearned: Working in a multidisciplinary team and building a complex mobile game using Unity. Developing a game from concept to polished prototype.
approach: I was the development lead for the project, so I designed most of the core systems and architecture, while also contributing to the game design. We quickly iterated in an agile manner using Kanban to manage our art and programming pipelines, while keeping a strict deadline for the prototype.

title: Useless Vending Machine - Big Mode Game Jam 2026
description: A game made in Unity for the Big Mode Game Jam 2026, solo project.
thingsLearned: I participated on two game jams on two consecutive weekends. From this project I learned a lot about scope and time management, since I wanted to make a game that was memorable. I focused on how audio design directly drives game feel, turning a short loop into a highly responsive and funny experience.
approach: I started by scoping my time and designing the core experience. I went with a smaller gameplay loop so that it could be the most polished possible within the 3 days that I had. I made all the audio with my mouth, which was a fun challenge, while also making all the mechanics work with minimal bugs.

title: Neil-A's Big Halloween - Global Game Jam 2026
description: A Unity story driven game made in a team of 7 for the Global Game Jam 2026.
thingsLearned: Working with a team that I just met and making a game in 3 days. We used Yarn, a dialogue system for Unity, which taught me how to set up an efficient workflow that allowed us to import massive amounts of narrative content without breaking our core scripts.
approach: We started brainstorming around the theme of Mask, while also keeping our team's skills in mind. We ended up with a more narrative experience with a lot of dialogue, so after the main mechanics were done on the second day, we spent the rest of the time adding the dialogue and polishing the game.
linkText: View on the Global Game Jam page

title: A Disadvantageous Adventure - Solo project
description: An incremental game made in Unity, solo project.
thingsLearned: Scoping for personal projects. Make a mobile game from scratch in Unity using touch and mouse inputs to interact with the game through phone and computer respectively.
approach: While ideating for the Pocket Flock project I wanted to make a proof-of-concept to test how developing a mobile game would work. I scoped the project for 2 weeks, making a short experience with simple interactions. I focused on making the dice rolling feel natural, while balancing the incremental math of the upgrades to keep the progression satisfying.

title: Meownshine Express Co. - Game Design course project
description: A simulation game made in Unity with a team of 6.
thingsLearned: This was the first game I made, so I learned the process of designing a game, bringing it to life in Unity and working with a team.
approach: Since this was for a class, we brainstormed ideas and came up with the concept and iterated on it. A prototype was made to test some mechanics and then full production for a final presentation. Learning Unity between Youtube videos, documentation, and using AI as a guide was a great way to get this 2-month project done in an efficient way.

title: Final Stand - Unreal Engine course project
description: A Blackjack versus AI game made in Unreal, solo project for an Unreal Engine course.
thingsLearned: Learning how to mix C++ and Blueprints in Unreal Engine. I got a lot of practical experience setting up UI layouts, using simple timelines to make card animations feel more satisfying, and building a basic state machine to drive the opponent's AI.
approach: This game was made in 3 weeks for a course, in which I had to scope and decide which features to develop. I focused heavily on the C++ side to better understand how to pass information over to Blueprints, letting C++ handle the backend rules of the card game while Blueprints managed the UI and visual feedback.
